paper.title_en: Phenomenological constraints on matter-antimatter asymmetry phenomenon in spatially curved FRW $f(Q)$ gravity
paper.abstract_en: In this study, we explore the gravitational baryogenesis mechanism within the context of f(Q) gravity, where Q is a non-metricity scalar. We consider a special case of this theory which demonstrate the universe spatially curved FRW model by considering a variable temporal function γ(t). For Underlying framework, we examine two distinct forms of f(Q) models: (i) <math altimg="si102.svg"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>α</mi><msup><mi>Q</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></math> (power law form), (ii) <math altimg="si103.svg"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mi>β</mi><msup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> (quadratic polynomial). We also discuss the different cases of γ(t) for these two models. We investigate the baryon asymmetry by calculating the dimensionless ratio <math altimg="si104.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mi>s</mi></mfrac></mrow></math>, where ηB represents the baryon number density while s reflects the universe’s entropy density. We compare our theoretical predictions for the baryon-to-entropy ratio, YB, to the observed restriction of <math altimg="si105.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>9.42</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Our numerical results confirm the experimentally known value, indicating that our modified gravitational framework may explain the observed baryon asymmetry in the cosmos.
